LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to write legibly and neatly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication
2. write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication
3. appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting to a partner. (skill: write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to write legibly and neatly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication.
5. Be able to: write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
